detail: SB 2807 took effect Sep 1, 2025; rules finalized Feb 2026, enforcement began May 28, 2026. Tesla received a statewide TDLR transportation-network-company permit in Aug 2025 (initial term to Aug 6, 2026) covering supervised and unsupervised operation; service has continued past that date.

Requires DMV permits for testing/deployment (with and without a safety driver) plus a separate CPUC permit to actually charge for rides. Tesla holds a testing permit and a CPUC charter-party carrier permit, but not yet a full driverless deployment permit as of mid-2026.

framework: Light-touch, no AV-specific permit regime found
detail: Uses a lighter self-certification process for testing (granted Sep 2025) plus a statewide Transportation Network Company permit for paid rides (granted Nov 2025, approved in 4 days) — unlike California's city-by-city geofenced permits, Arizona's TNC authorization covers the entire state at once.

detail: Reporting describes Florida as not requiring a specific AV permit, though this is lower-confidence (sourced to community/forum discussion rather than a regulatory filing) and worth treating as provisional.

framework: Capped at 10, then opened to 5,000 — plus Zoox's federal first
detail: Tesla filed Jun 5, 2026 for an AVNC permit to run up to 5,000 vehicles across Clark County. The state first granted it Jul 27 with a 10-vehicle interim cap on the Strip — then on Aug 20 the Nevada Transportation Authority expanded it to up to 5,000 vehicles county-wide (airport still needs separate approval). Tesla has not yet launched public rides there. Waymo opened paid public service in Las Vegas Sep 14. Separately, on Jul 30, Zoox became the first company ever to win a federal NHTSA exemption for a robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals — cleared to charge fares on up to 2,500 vehicles/year; paid rides began Aug 10.
